minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted a special permit letting 436 Massachusetts Ave be used as a two-bedroom home, unanimously.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard an application for a special permit (dimensional variation) to convert the former Hearthstone real estate office at 436 Massachusetts Avenue, in the commercial district, back to a single-family residence because the lot is under the required area. The board read the application, building inspector and Board of Health letters, took comments, and granted the permit unanimously with a two-bedroom restriction. A member afterward questioned whether the permit should lapse on sale.

public_comment.topic: Applicant gave name and address and said his application covers what he wishes to convey.
Spoke in support of the applicant's character and care of the property.
A speaker said town sewer ends at Caswell antique shop and extending it past that point was previously judged too costly.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit for dimensional variation for 436 Massachusetts Ave with the stipulation that it be a two-bedroom dwelling.

budget_items.what_was_said: A speaker recalled the town and contractors estimated the cost of extending sewer to the neighbourhood as too high for the few properties served.

decisions.decision: Permit granted subject to compliance with all local, state and federal regulations (including the Board of Health letter), personal to the applicant, ending if sold or sublet, and lapsing in two years without substantial use.
Two-bedroom restriction to be recorded on the deed as a stipulation of approval.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously granted a special permit for 436 Massachusetts Ave to be used as a single-family home, limited to two bedrooms.
The permit was needed because the lot is under the required area; the building was formerly a real estate office in the commercial district.
The permit is personal to the applicant, ends if the property is sold or sublet, and lapses in two years without substantial use.
The two-bedroom limit is to be recorded on the deed as a condition of approval, and the permit requires compliance with the Board of Health letter.
Speakers said sewer service ends short of the property and an extension was earlier judged too costly for the few properties served.

why_it_matters: The two-bedroom limit recorded on the deed and the sewer and septic questions show how a lot-size permit can set lasting limits on a property that is not on town sewer.
A member asked whether the permit should lapse on sale, so residents with similar properties should note that this permit was made personal to the applicant.
watch_next: The two-year lapse date on the permit if the home is not put to substantial use.
